title: Compatible coefficient models and finite-Tor domain for compact support
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$ and $e\geq1$ with $tB=v^eB$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete bounded constructible category with a uniform Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $A_n=A/t^n$, $B_n=B/t^nB=B/v^{en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$. For $H=E,F$, let $P_H^c$ be the integral compact-support functor attached to $c$, defined as the total derived inverse limit of its finite separately derived proper/open images [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

The rings $A$ and $B$ are complete for their uniformizer-adic topologies; $\bigcap_n t^nB=0$, and $B$ has an $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ inducing compatible $A_n$-bases of $B_n$. Under restriction from completed coefficient sheaves to constant ring sheaves, the derived-complete categories, their quotient diagrams, quotient transitions and total derived inverse limits are identified canonically. In this model $C_W$ on complete objects is scalar extension by the finite free constant module $\underline B_W$, with ordinary-tensor/strict-tower comparison $\chi$ normalized by the quotient product map and zero shifted-product component [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. These identifications commute with the coefficient inverse-image maps for every scheme morphism and with finite quotient maps. The ambient native derived localization tensor and its K-flat representative tensor have the same canonical associator and unit comparisons [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor].

The object $C_XM$ is derived complete and bounded constructible and has the same uniform Tor bounds as $M$. More explicitly, for every $a\geq1$ and $en\geq a$ there is the canonical balanced-tensor identification
$$ (C_XM)\otimes^L_{S_X}(B/v^a)_X\cong M_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}(B/v^a)_X,$$
and for every degree-zero $(B/v^a)_X$-module $N$, further tensoring is canonically $M_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}N$, with $N$ restricted to $A_n$. The integral compact-support values $P_E^cM$ and $P_F^c(C_XM)$ lie in the derived-complete bounded constructible categories on $Y$, where $P_E^c$ and $P_F^c$ are the reduction-limit functors of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. These assertions do not require smoothness or a purity isomorphism.

proof.text: For either coefficient field H, use finite_module_adic_complete_and_hom on its integer ring. Its bijective canonical adic-completion map implies IsAdicComplete by AdicCompletion.of_bijective_iff. For separatedness, ramification and Ideal.map_pow rewrite the mapped nth ideal as (v^e)^n. The DVR maximal ideal is generated by v; since e is positive, (v^e) is contained in that proper maximal ideal. Apply the Krull-intersection lemma Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing.

source.place: Opening sentence; elementary completeness/separatedness argument from the cited valued-field facts.

proof.text: Use the public local-field integral-basis theorem with the actual scalar absolute-value compatibility. Its unique coordinate expansions give a bijective linear coordinate map and hence a Module.Basis; this is the private coefficientIntegralBasis argument with the two scalar algebra instances. Its basis coordinate equivalence is the displayed sum of scalar multiples. For every n, ramification identifies the target ideal with the image of the source ideal. Base-change that same basis to the source quotient and transport it along the standard quotient tensor equivalence; the private coefficientQuotientBasis proof records the generator formula. The inverse quotient-coordinate equivalence gives the requested coordinates; surjectivity of the quotient map supplies lifts, and injectivity of the coordinate equivalence proves uniqueness. This works also at n=0. The ordinary constant-module model still uses the basis/limit argument described in the following step.

source.place: Opening basis construction, realized with the actual inverse-limit coefficient sheaves.

proof.text: Use the noetherian instance in the actual coefficient datum. The existing completed_constant_presentation_transport supplies the presentation transport. ConstantCompletion.equivalence, derivedReductionTowerComparison and derivedLimitRestriction supply the category equivalence, normalized tower comparison with all transitions, and derived-limit comparison with its counit. The completed and strict inverse-image squares are already in the coefficient-data declarations; the arbitrary quotient square is proEtaleConstantInverseImageMap_naturality for the explicitly constructed quotient ring homomorphism.

source.place: Section derived-completion-noetherian; Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), using sites-modules Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat) and algebraization Tag 099I (lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence).

proof.text: Obtain component isomorphisms with their pure-tensor formulas from the ordinary-existence node. Build a natural isomorphism using NatIso.ofComponents: tensor-generator extensionality reduces naturality to pure tensors, where naturality of scalar extension and the component formulas prove the equation. The same extensionality argument proves uniqueness. The helper supplies objectwise basis comparisons only; the parent proves their naturality and uniqueness.

source.place: Basis-induced scalar identification; balanced tensor formula on the constant/completed presentations.

proof.text: For a derived-complete input, apply finiteFreeCompletedScalarComparison. Its scalar comparison is the prescribed completedScalarComparison, not an arbitrary isomorphism. The choose_spec of completedScalarComparison_existsUnique gives exactly the quotient-product normalization; the choose_spec of completedScalarChainComparison_existsUnique gives its chain-level zero shifted-product component.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1) for coefficient realization; specified ordinary/strict-tower comparison supplied by the cited DAG lemma.

proof.text: For moduleBalancing, the existing inverse ordinaryTensorCancellation comparison has the required section formula. Uniqueness follows by precomposing with its inverse and using tensor-generator extensionality through the module sheafification adjunction. The quotient square and balanced reduction remain as proved. For furtherTensor, specialize the existing ordinaryTensorCancellation to pbcExtend at the retained quotient map, using its object and map identifications. Its inverse has the moduleBalancing normalization and therefore equals the chosen unique module map. Its naturality with the second module fixed gives a natural isomorphism between the two termwise tensor functors. Apply NatIso.mapHomologicalComplex, and conjugate by mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso on source and target to obtain the chain isomorphism. Its degreewise equation is the stated normalization. Compose the fixed mapDerivedCategoryFactors with DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso of this chain isomorphism. Any other witness has the same chain components after cancellation of the target mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso, hence the same chain isomorphism and the same localization. No flatness or positivity is needed for this chain-level identity; in particular the existing K-flat hypothesis is retained but unused. The native associator and unitor clauses still refer to the proved RingedDerivedNative comparisons.

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); native localization normalization from lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor.

proof.text: Convert the intrinsic completeness of the input to the legacy integralCtfProperty using sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy. Rewrite the stated ramification equality at level one into the principal-ideal equality expected by purAdicScalarExtensionTorBound. Apply that theorem to obtain preservation of every common Tor interval, and apply it again to the interval supplied by the input to recover the finiteTorConstructibleIntegral bounds.

source.place: Step 1 finite-Tor lattice domain; elementary application of the Tor definition to the balanced formula of Step 6.

proof.text: Apply sfIntegralScalarExtension_constructible to the input intrinsic constructible object. To apply finiteFreeCompletedScalarComparison at its legacy unrestricted interface, choose a prime different from l and construct a small finite-field datum; sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy supplies the required completeness witness. The comparison is thus an isomorphism at M. The intrinsic constructible property is closed under isomorphism, so transport constructibility from the strict-tower scalar extension to pbcDerivedExtend. Combine with the unchanged Tor interval from the preceding step. No Noetherian or dimension comparison is needed in this assembly.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1), constructible integral coefficient models; stratified-perfect and scalar-transport interfaces stated in the cited DAG nodes.

proof.text: Apply the proved scalar clause to M. The existing normalized sfQcqsCompactSupportRealization_existsUnique, once for E and once for F, identifies the two ambient proper/open images with values of the actual constructible integral compact-support functors. Their values have the constructible property by their codomain. Transport this property across each realization isomorphism using closure under isomorphisms. At E, compose the same realization component with sfCompactSupportFiniteIntegralFunctor_obj to obtain the displayed value comparison. Retain the two specification and uniqueness proofs verbatim for the final two conjuncts.
